newsitem.title: FRANCE: French shares end firm, off highs.
newsitem.headline: French shares end firm, off highs.

text.p: French shares firmed to a fresh record close Thursday but came off the day's high after being dented by the U.S. Chicago Purchasing Managers Index that stoked inflationary fears, traders said.

But dollar strength provided underlying support for the market, a broker said. Low long-term French interest rates were also seen positive for company earnings, especially cyclical stocks. Continuing high unemployment in France made it unlikely rates would rise, he added.
National statistics institute INSEE reported June saw a rise of 17,400 on the jobless rolls, bringing the unemployment rate to a record 12.6 percent, based on a new method of calculation.
Volume was an exceptionally high 17 billion francs, inflated by expiry of the July futures and options contracts.
The CAC-40 index closed up 6.37, or 0.21 percent, at 3,075.67.
The CAC-40 July futures closed at 3,103 versus 3,072 at Wednesday's close.
The broader SBF120 index was up 8.12 at 2,097.41
Underlying market activity was expected to slow in the coming days, as London fund managers start to take off for August holidays, drying up the flow of investment decisions, a broker said.
Alcatel Alsthom closed up 2.28 percent at 809. The company reported first-half sales up 17 percent at 86.92 billion francs.
PSA Peugeot Citroen shot ahead with a 4.07 percent gain to 716, benefiting from broker upgrades after its 6.3 percent rise in first-half sales.
A number of block trades helped push up volumes, among them 557,000 Elf Aquitaine shares, 214,000 Sanofi, 489,000 Renault, 330,000 Alcatel, 673,000 Axa, 680,000 Rhone-Poulenc and 496,000 Usinor.

Nickel producer Eramet closed up 3.68 percent at 335. Shareholders approved Yves Rambaud as board member at the annual meeting, at which he forecast first half profits would be at least the same level as the year ago level.
BIC ran into profit-taking, off 0.78 percent at 511, after hitting a day high of 511 on the back of its planned U.S. Sheaffer pen acquisition.

Renault softened 0.17 percent to 172.4. The carmaker said it would it would sell its remaining three percent Volvo stake at the right time, following confirmation by the Swedish company that it had sold its 11.38 percent Renault holding.
